headline: Sequencing-based copy number and variant effect calling under realistic benchmarking
label: Genomic Variant Interpretation Methods
summary: Recent preprints and publications extend variant interpretation to repetitive regions, FFPE artifacts, and calibrated pathogenicity scoring.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational interpretation of variants from exome and genome sequencing, with emphasis on calibration and benchmarking against realistic ground truth. CHALLENGER applies masked language modeling to short-read depth to detect copy number variants in repetitive regions, and ExactCN predicts exact per-exon copy numbers from whole exome data with a CNN plus transformer trained on WGS semi-ground truth. Floco performs copy number calling on genome graphs via a network flow formulation. RaCoon proposes residue-level, subgroup-specific calibration of ESM1b-based variant effect scores, while V2P conditions SNV and indel pathogenicity on 23 HPO disease phenotypes. VSPGx extends interpretation to pharmacogenomics. Artifact-aware and benchmarking studies, including FFPErase for FFPE-derived WGS and a DNA methylation deconvolution benchmark, test performance under realistic conditions. The set is heterogeneous, so this reflects the dominant theme rather than a shared method.
